skill.name: vibe-security
skill.description: Security analysis skill for scanning code, dependencies, configuration, and common web vulnerabilities across several languages.
skill.summary: Scan application code for common security vulnerabilities and practical remediation guidance.
skill.author: 0x8506

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from scanner signatures, CSV examples, markdown code fences, and fixed-argument helper commands. I confirmed the elevated sudo install instruction and added semantic findings for unescaped HTML reports and unbounded auto-fix writes.

remediation.issue: Elevated package installation guidance in SKILL.md
remediation.suggestion: Remove sudo and system package installation commands from the skill, or require explicit user confirmation before running them.

remediation.issue: HTML report fields are not escaped
remediation.suggestion: Escape all vulnerability fields before HTML insertion, or use a template engine with automatic escaping enabled.

remediation.issue: Auto-fix target paths are not constrained to the project root
remediation.suggestion: Resolve target paths and reject writes outside the configured project path. Make dry-run and user confirmation the default path.

remediation.issue: Scanner data contains many dangerous example tokens
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples in structured fixtures with clear scanner-ignore metadata to reduce audit noise.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped HTML Report Rendering
semantic_findings.description: The HTML report inserts vulnerability type, file, message, code, and remediation fields directly into markup. Scan results can contain untrusted project content, so opening the report can trigger stored XSS.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The report builder directly interpolates vulnerability fields into HTML and preformatted blocks without escaping. These fields can come from scanned source files or tool output.

semantic_findings.title: Auto-Fix Writes Outside Project Boundary
semantic_findings.description: The auto-fix helper converts a supplied filepath directly to a path and writes replacement content after a fuzzy line match. It does not enforce that the target stays under the configured project path.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code uses Path(filepath) directly and later writes fixed content to that path. The matching check reduces accidental writes but does not provide path containment.

content.value_statement: Security defects are hard to find during fast development. This skill checks code, dependencies, and configurations for common risks and suggests focused fixes.
actual_capabilities: Searches a security knowledge base for vulnerabilities, rules, frameworks, and language patterns.
Analyzes Python files with AST checks for injection, deserialization, SQL, and command risks.
Checks JavaScript and TypeScript files with heuristic patterns for XSS, SQL injection, and unsafe execution.
Runs dependency audit helpers for npm, Python, Go, and Rust projects when matching files exist.
Suggests remediation templates and security tests for common vulnerability classes.
Generates security reports in HTML, JSON, CSV, and SARIF formats.
limitations: Pattern and heuristic checks can miss vulnerabilities that require full application context.
Dependency scanning depends on external tools being installed and available on the system path.
Auto-fix suggestions require human review before changes are trusted in production.
The skill does not replace a professional penetration test or threat model.

use_cases.title: Review Web Application Changes
use_cases.description: Find SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, authentication, and authorization issues before a pull request is merged.

use_cases.title: Audit Dependencies Before Release
use_cases.description: Check package manifests for known vulnerabilities and summarize upgrade priorities by ecosystem.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Map findings to OWASP, CWE, MITRE ATT&CK, NIST, and PCI-DSS references for review workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Security Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for one project folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this project for common security issues. Prioritize critical and high findings, and explain each fix in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Specific Vulnerability
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of one risk class.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the authentication and session handling code. Identify bypass risks, weak cookies, missing MFA, and unsafe error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Fix Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these security findings and create a fix plan. Group fixes by severity, owner, test coverage, and release risk.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release security audit across code, dependencies, and infrastructure configuration. Produce an executive summary and developer actions.

output_examples.input: Scan an Express API for injection and authentication risks.
output: Critical: possible SQL injection in a user lookup path.
High: missing authorization check on an account update route.
Recommended next step: replace concatenated queries and add route-level access checks.

output_examples.input: Review dependency risk before a release.
output: Summary: three vulnerable packages need review before deployment.
Highest priority: update the package with remote code execution exposure.
Follow-up: rerun the dependency audit after upgrades are applied.

output_examples.input: Prepare a security report for a sprint review.
output: Report includes severity totals, affected files, remediation notes, and standards mapping.
The team should address critical findings before release approval.

best_practices: Run scans on a clean working tree so suggested fixes are easy to review.
Review every auto-fix manually and add tests that prove the vulnerability is closed.
Prioritize exploitable critical findings before broad cleanup or style changes.
anti_patterns: Do not apply generated fixes directly to production branches without review.
Do not treat a clean scan as proof that the application is secure.
Do not paste secrets or private customer data into prompts or reports.

faq.question: What languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It includes checks and guidance for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, PHP, Java, Go, Ruby, and several extended languages.

faq.question: Can it fix vulnerabilities automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest fixes and includes an auto-fix helper, but changes should be reviewed and tested before merge.

faq.question: Does it scan dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It can call ecosystem audit tools for npm, Python, Go, and Rust when those tools are installed.

faq.question: Does it support compliance reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. Its data maps common vulnerabilities to OWASP, CWE, MITRE ATT&CK, NIST, and PCI-DSS references.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: Use normal repository safeguards. Review commands before running external audit tools or writing generated reports.

faq.question: Can it replace a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It is useful for triage and developer review, but high-risk systems still need expert assessment.
